messages.content:
You are FOXO's lifestyle coach. Using the doctor's review of a member's lab results, write a practical diet and lifestyle plan for a member living in India.

Rules:
1. Respect the member's diet, allergies and conditions in every item:
   - vegetarian: no meat, fish, seafood or eggs
   - eggetarian: eggs are fine; no meat, fish or seafood
   - vegan: no animal products, including dairy, ghee and honey
   - jain: vegetarian with no eggs, no honey, no onion or garlic, and no root vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar)
   - allergies: never include the allergen in any form
   - diabetes: no sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets or sweetened drinks
2. Each diet recommendation must target one of the abnormal biomarkers in the doctor's findings. Put that biomarker's name in linked_biomarker, written as in the findings.
3. Never contradict the doctor's lifestyle_restrictions. If the doctor restricts exercise, suggest only gentle activity such as an easy walk, and tell the member to follow the doctor's advice.
4. Do not recommend medicines or supplements and never give doses. If a supplement might help, say "ask your FOXO doctor".
5. Use everyday Indian foods (dal, millets, seasonal sabzi, sprouts and so on) and be specific about portions and timing.
6. Put foods to eat in diet_recommendations and foods to limit or avoid in foods_to_avoid.
7. retest_in_weeks is usually 12.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"DietRecommendation": {"properties": {"item": {"title": "Item", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "linked_biomarker": {"title": "Linked Biomarker", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["item", "rationale", "linked_biomarker"], "title": "DietRecommendation", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"focus_areas": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Focus Areas", "type": "array"}, "diet_recommendations": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DietRecommendation"}, "title": "Diet Recommendations", "type": "array"}, "foods_to_avoid": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Foods To Avoid", "type": "array"}, "activity": {"title": "Activity", "type": "string"}, "sleep": {"title": "Sleep", "type": "string"}, "retest_in_weeks": {"title": "Retest In Weeks", "type": "integer"}}, "required": ["focus_areas", "diet_recommendations", "activity", "sleep", "retest_in_weeks"], "title": "CoachPlan", "type": "object"}

response: {"focus_areas":["Lower LDL cholesterol","Lower total cholesterol","Heart-healthy vegetarian eating","Regular physical activity","Weight and waist management"],"diet_recommendations":[{"item":"Breakfast 3–4 days/week: 1 bowl (30 g dry) rolled oats cooked in water or low-fat milk, topped with 1 tbsp roasted flaxseed powder and 1/2 cup seasonal fruit like apple, guava or papaya — no sugar. On other days: 2 ragi or jowar rotis with 1 cup dal.","rationale":"Oats and flaxseed provide soluble fibre that helps reduce LDL cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"},{"item":"Lunch daily: 2 jowar/bajra rotis or 1 cup cooked brown rice + 1 cup dal (moong/masoor/chana) + 1 cup seasonal sabzi + 1 small bowl salad. Add 1 cup cooked rajma or chana 3 times/week.","rationale":"Whole grains and pulses are high in fibre and replace refined grains, helping lower total cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"total_cholesterol"},{"item":"Mid-morning or evening snack: 1 cup boiled/steamed moong or chana sprouts with lemon and chaat masala, or 4–5 unsalted almonds + 2 walnuts. Avoid fried snacks at this time.","rationale":"Plant protein and unsalted nuts support a better lipid profile and help lower LDL cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"},{"item":"Dinner before 8 pm: 1 cup millet khichdi (bajra/jowar/ragi) or 2 phulkas + 1 cup dal + 1 cup cooked seasonal sabzi. Keep dinner light and avoid topping with ghee or butter.","rationale":"A high-fibre, low-saturated-fat dinner helps lower total cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"total_cholesterol"},{"item":"Use only 2 teaspoons total cooking oil per day (mustard, rice bran or olive oil); prefer steaming, boiling, grilling or sautéing with minimal oil. Include 1 small bowl of low-fat curd or buttermilk with lunch.","rationale":"Reducing saturated fat and total oil intake helps lower LDL cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"}],"foods_to_avoid":["Deep-fried foods such as samosa, pakora, puri, bhujia, chips and fried namkeen","Sweets, mithai, sugar, jaggery, honey, sweetened drinks and fruit juices","Refined carbohydrates such as maida, white bread, bakery biscuits, cakes and large portions of white rice","Full-fat paneer, butter, ghee, cream and large amounts of whole milk","Coconut oil, palm oil, vanaspati and repeated reused frying oil","Processed and packaged foods, instant noodles and salty packaged snacks"],"activity":"With no exercise restriction from your doctor, aim for a brisk walk of 30–40 minutes on 5 days a week, plus 10 minutes of light stretching or yoga daily. Start slowly and stop if you feel chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness; follow your doctor’s advice.","sleep":"Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep each night. Keep a fixed sleep and wake time, avoid screens for 1 hour before bed, and avoid heavy late meals.","retest_in_weeks":12}
